chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Ibrahim ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Khalaf, from Musa ibn Ibrahim al-Marwazi, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding two horses that collided, so one of them died; therefore, he made the remaining one liable for the blood-money (diyah) of the dead one.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Who is liable for the blood-money if two animals collide and one dies?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) establishes the principle of *kafalah* (guarantee/liability) in animal collisions, ruling that the surviving animal's owner bears the *diyah* for the deceased. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it clarifies that liability attaches to the animal itself rather than requiring proof of fault or negligence by the owner, reflecting a strict liability approach in commercial and property disputes.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Kufy, from Ibrahim Bin Al Hassan, from Muhammad Bin Khalaf, from Musa Bin Ibrahim Al Marouzy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding two horses collided, so one of the two dies. So the responsibility is upon the (owner of the) remaining one, wergild of the dead (horse)’.
